ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
2-day history of decreased urine output and generalized weakness following bloody diarrhea 1 week ago

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the Emergency Department one week after initial presentation with fever, abdominal cramping, and bloody diarrhea following consumption of undercooked hamburger. The child had an episode of bloody diarrhea 1 week ago, which resolved spontaneously.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli infection (EHEC/STEC) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

His immunizations are up to date.

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of chronic kidney disease
- No family history of autoimmune disorders
- No family history of hematologic disorders
- No family history of inflammatory bowel disease

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Pre-kindergarten student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is 95/60 mmHg, heart rate is 118 beats per minute, and temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears lethargic. Physical examination reveals pallor and mild edema of the lower extremities.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies are as follows:

- Hemoglobin: 7.8 g/dL (Normal: 11.5-13.5 g/dL)
- Platelet count: 45,000/mm³ (Normal: 150,000-400,000/mm³)
- Serum creatinine: 2.6 mg/dL (Normal: 0.3-0.7 mg/dL)
- Blood urea nitrogen (BUN): 45 mg/dL (Normal: 7-20 mg/dL)
- Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH): Elevated
- Peripheral blood smear: Presence of schistocytes

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever, abdominal cramping, and bloody diarrhea for 2 days after consuming undercooked hamburger at a picnic

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He is brought to the emergency department by his parents due to a 2-day history of fever, abdominal cramping, and bloody diarrhea. The parents report that the symptoms started a few hours after the family attended a picnic where the boy consumed a hamburger.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His past medical history is unremarkable, and his immunizations are up to date.

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of chronic kidney disease
- No family history of autoimmune disorders
- No family history of hematologic disorders
- No family history of inflammatory bowel disease

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Pre-kindergarten student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), heart rate is 110/min, and blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears lethargic but is not dehydrated. Abdominal examination reveals diffuse tenderness without rebound or guarding.

LABORATORY DATA:
The complete blood count shows a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, leukocyte count of 15,000/µL with a left shift, and platelets of 250,000/µL.

OTHER STUDIES:
A stool sample is obtained and sent for culture.
